status_note: Seen on 30.22.0, the release uv.lock pins; not yet checked against the latest release or searched upstream.
summary: SQLGlot parses a chain of set operations left to right at one level of precedence: `a UNION ALL b INTERSECT ALL c` reads as `(a UNION ALL b) INTERSECT ALL c`. SQL, DuckDB and Spark bind INTERSECT tighter than UNION and EXCEPT, `a UNION ALL (b INTERSECT ALL c)`, so the tree means other rows than the engines give. The DuckDB and Spark dialects both read it so.
repro:
```python
import sqlglot
t = sqlglot.parse_one("SELECT x FROM a EXCEPT SELECT x FROM b UNION ALL SELECT x FROM a INTERSECT ALL SELECT x FROM b", read="duckdb")
type(t).__name__, type(t.this).__name__  # ('Intersect', 'Union')
```
observed: the root is the INTERSECT. With a = {1, 1, 2, 3} and b = {1, 2, 2}, DuckDB 2.0.0 gives {1, 2, 3} (INTERSECT first) and the left-to-right reading gives {1, 2}.
handling: The SQL lift refuses an INTERSECT whose left operand is an unparenthesised UNION or EXCEPT, naming the parentheses that keep the meaning (`_check_set_precedence`); a parenthesised operand is a subquery to SQLGlot and lifts as written.
